label: Real run on this Mac's kind cluster (Kubernetes in Docker, from our own manifests in deploy/kind), with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, duplicate-delivery, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, offered one write action (rollback_deploy), which runs only if a person approves it at the gate, and stopped on diagnosed after 6 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Klaxon asked at the approval gate to act on its diagnosis; the request was approved with make approve (the request's id typed at a terminal), and the action ran: redeploy ledger-consumer: LEDGER_HANDLER naive -> idempotent, LEDGER_BAD_EVENTS dead_letter (unchanged). Code, not the model, then verified it (klaxon.agent.verify): passed; the cause is removed, and the money is not right. The fault's cause was removed by Klaxon: its rollback (Klaxon, approved request r-65be) removed the cause, and the harness's clearing then found the good settings running, and changed nothing.

fault.name: duplicate-delivery
fault.title: Payments counted twice in the books
fault.cause: a deploy of the ledger consumer without its dedupe (LEDGER_HANDLER=naive): every webhook the provider sends again, after an acknowledgement it never got, is booked a second time
expected_symptoms: the money check fails: events counted twice, the books ahead of the provider by their amounts
the webhook dashboard stays green, and consumer lag stays at 0
the ledger stops reporting 'already processed' while the confirmer still sees the same duplicates
fault.remedy: roll the ledger consumer back to the idempotent handler, then repair each double posting with a reversal (a write, so it needs approval)

diagnosis.hypothesis: ledger-consumer was redeployed at 21:45:59 (revision 2) with LEDGER_HANDLER=naive. That handler does not deduplicate by provider event_id. The provider resends webhooks until they are acknowledged, so the same event can reach provider-events more than once. Each copy lands at its own Kafka offset, and the naive handler posts a new ledger transaction for every copy. Example: evt_000308 arrived at offsets 100, 101 and 103 and was posted 3 times. Because each duplicate is a balanced double entry, ledger_balanced still passes. posted_exactly_once fails, though, and the provider_clearing balance runs $461.00 ahead of the provider. Duplicated payment.succeeded events inflate it. A duplicated refund (evt_000288, pay_000217) pushes that payment's balance below the provider's. Still open: I did not check whether duplicates occurred before 21:45:59, or why the provider's figure for pay_000240 shows $0. That charge may be newer than the provider's cutoff.

evidence.shows: The money check fails posted_exactly_once with 7 events posted 2-3 times each, and matches_provider with the ledger +$461.00 vs the provider. The ledger is balanced, and our payments and refunds match the provider.
ledger-consumer was redeployed at 21:45:59, 17s before the alert, as revision 2 with LEDGER_HANDLER=naive. Every other service is unchanged at revision 1.
ledger-consumer logged 'posted' for evt_000308 three times (21:46:12-21:46:14), from Kafka offsets 100, 101 and 103, each with its own trace. Redelivered copies were not skipped.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll ledger-consumer back to its previous revision so it again posts each event_id at most once. Then repair the data separately: reverse the extra ledger transactions listed by the money check (e.g. 255, 265, 272, 273, 297 and the other duplicates) and re-run the money check.

diagnosis.blast_radius: ledger-consumer pauses while its container is recreated, so ledger posting lags briefly. Events queue in Kafka and are consumed on restart. payment-confirmer and the payment flow are unaffected. The rollback does not remove the duplicates already booked, which need a data repair.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Redeploy ledger-consumer with the current revision-2 settings (LEDGER_HANDLER=naive). This is not advisable, though: watch the money check and consumer lag after the rollback instead.

printed_output: Klaxon week 4: a gated run on a fault: duplicate-delivery

Real run on this Mac's kind cluster (Kubernetes in Docker, from our own manifests in deploy/kind), with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, duplicate-delivery, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, offered one write action (rollback_deploy), which runs only if a person approves it at the gate, and stopped on diagnosed after 6 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Klaxon asked at the approval gate to act on its diagnosis; the request was approved with make approve (the request's id typed at a terminal), and the action ran: redeploy ledger-consumer: LEDGER_HANDLER naive -> idempotent, LEDGER_BAD_EVENTS dead_letter (unchanged). Code, not the model, then verified it (klaxon.agent.verify): passed; the cause is removed, and the money is not right. The fault's cause was removed by Klaxon: its rollback (Klaxon, approved request r-65be) removed the cause, and the harness's clearing then found the good settings running, and changed nothing.
